summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — PTC +33%, CTVA +13%, ILMN +8%, CRL +7%, GLW +6%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (CHRW -11%, STX -10%, MRNA -7%, WDC -7%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: PTC (+33.49%) — Schneider Electric agreed to buy PTC for $205/share in cash (~$22.6B, 42% premium). The stock gapped up about 33% and closed at $192.26, about 6% below the offer price. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: PTC is a ~$20B mid/large-cap industrial software name. It was an overnight M&A gap, so a post-open momentum or news-reactive entry had no tradable edge. A cash-deal target also trades pinned near the offer.

top_movers.catalyst: Schneider Electric agreed to buy PTC for $205/share in cash (~$22.6B, 42% premium). The stock gapped up about 33% and closed at $192.26, about 6% below the offer price.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: PTC is a ~$20B mid/large-cap industrial software name. It was an overnight M&A gap, so a post-open momentum or news-reactive entry had no tradable edge. A cash-deal target also trades pinned near the offer.
top_movers.suggestion: No actionable change. A cash takeover gap has capped upside and no momentum follow-through. If wanted, add an M&A-news flag that blocks new entries in cash-deal targets rather than chasing them.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed same-day news found. The Oct 1 Corteva/Vylor separation was on track, and a 14.025 close (vs ~$80 pre-spin) suggests a post-spin price rebase. The +13.2% may be partly a spin-related artifact.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CTVA is a mid/large-cap ag-chemicals/seeds name that no strategy lists. The post-spin price discontinuity and new ticker/share structure would also distort gap, RSI and volume-baseline filters.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a corporate-action guard: when a spin-off or split is detected, rebuild the price/volume baselines and keep the name out of gap-up filters for about 5 sessions. Also add large-cap Materials/Ag names to the momentum universe, or no change if the move is an artifact.

top_movers.catalyst: No company-specific news found for Oct 7. ILMN is in a momentum run on analyst target hikes (RBC Outperform), an AI-infrastructure sequencing narrative, a raised FY EPS outlook and its S&P 500 inclusion (Sept 21).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ILMN is a mid-cap life-science tools name, now S&P 500, that no strategy lists. With no discrete catalyst, a news-reactive bot had no trigger. It was also extended after a run from ~$158 in May to ~$294.
top_movers.suggestion: Add recent S&P 500 additions (e.g. the last 60 days) to the momentum-trader universe, and add a 20-day relative-strength rank, so sustained analyst-driven trend names like ILMN qualify without needing a news trigger.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely follow-through from the Investor Day: 2030 targets (5-7% organic growth CAGR), a raised 2026 outlook and price-target hikes (Jefferies 305→340). I couldn't confirm a news item dated Oct 7 itself.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CRL is a ~$13-15B mid-cap life-science/CRO name. The move was driven by an analyst and guidance catalyst that had already started building before the session, so there was no fresh gap signal.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a mid-cap healthcare/life-science tools watchlist (market cap ≥$5B, 20-day average dollar volume ≥$50M) to the momentum universe, plus an analyst-PT-raise or Investor-Day event trigger.

top_movers.catalyst: No same-day news found. Likely a sympathy move in AI optical/fiber names, since GLW has been driven by AI data-center demand (Meta deal up to $6B) and has had 23 moves over 5% in the past year.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. GLW is a large-cap industrial/optical-components name that none of the strategies' universe lists include. With no identifiable catalyst, a news-reactive bot would also have had no trigger.
top_movers.suggestion: Add high-beta AI-infrastructure large caps (GLW, ANET, COHR, CIEN) to the momentum-trader universe, or lift its universe filter to include any S&P 500 name with 20-day ATR% above 3%.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for 2026-10-07; likely an AI/semiconductor sector rally lifting MRVL (+5.9%). Searches turned up no company-specific news for that day.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: MRVL is a large-cap (recently S&P 500) semiconductor name that no strategy lists. With no news trigger, the move looks like sector beta that a news-reactive bot had nothing to react to.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap semis (MRVL, AVGO, AMD, etc.) to the momentum-trader universe, or add a sector-relative-strength screen that admits any S&P 500 name up ≥5% on above-average volume.

top_movers.catalyst: Continued selloff after CHRW's announced ~$5.8B acquisition of rival broker RXO (investor dilution and overcapacity worries; BofA cut its target to $203). Day-specific cause not confirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe (mid-cap freight broker, not in any strategy's list). It was also a multi-day, deal-driven drop after an announcement gap, so post-open momentum or mean-reversion signals fired late or not at all.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a news-reactive watchlist rule that admits any S&P 400/500 name with a ≥8% one-day drop on M&A news to the mean-reversion universe, with a 2-day cooldown to avoid catching a falling knife.

top_movers.catalyst: No company-specific news found. STX fell 9.6% to 802 in what looks like a sector-wide AI-storage/HDD selloff (WDC, SNDK and memory names also weak). The searches didn't confirm a same-day trigger.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: STX is a ~$800/share, large-cap hardware name that no strategy lists. The drop was a sector sell-off with no earnings or gap catalyst, so no news-reactive signal fired. A long-only bot can't express a down move anyway.
top_movers.suggestion: No actionable change for this one, since it needs short capability. Optionally add AI-storage/memory names (STX, WDC, SNDK, MU) to the momentum universe, so sector-wide drawdowns trigger exit or avoid-entry signals.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found for Oct 7. Searches turned up no MRNA-specific news that day, so this is likely a sector or technical move after a sharp run-up (about $154 in mid-Sept to $189).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: MRNA is a volatile mid-cap biotech that no strategy's universe includes. Even if it were included, a drop after a big run-up with no news would not trigger momentum or news-reactive entries.
top_movers.suggestion: (no actionable change: a long-only bot can't express a no-news biotech drop.) If wanted, add a mean-reversion watchlist for names that rose >20% in 3 weeks and then fell >5% on volume above 1.5× average.

top_movers.catalyst: No obvious news catalyst found. Searches turned up nothing dated 2026-10-07, so this is likely a sector-wide pullback in storage/AI-hardware names after a big run (close 411).
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: WDC is a large-cap hard-drive/storage name that no strategy includes. A -6.9% drop with no catalyst also wouldn't trigger a news-reactive rule, and a long-only bot can't short it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add WDC and peers (STX, MU, SNDK) to the mean-reversion universe, gated on a ≥5% one-day drop with no earnings in the last 3 days. Otherwise no change, since the bot can't short.
